nodes.title: Inject Video Latent
widgets_values:
WHY THIS NODE EXISTS

H3's stock nodes ALWAYS build a zeros latent. References are conditioning that is re-injected every step - never a starting point. So there is no video-to-video path out of the box.

This encodes the real cropped frames into the VIDEO stream of the joint AV latent, leaving the audio stream alone. That turns SamplerCustomAdvanced + denoise<1.0 into ordinary img2img.

Frame count must sit on H3's 17k+5 grid (5, 22, 39 ... 175, 226, 362). Clips generated by H3 already do.

nodes.title: READ ME FIRST
widgets_values:
WHY THIS EXISTS

MiniMax H3 renders faces poorly when the head is a SMALL FRACTION OF THE FRAME. That is a property of head-size-in-frame, not of resolution - it persists at 720p and above.

So no upscaler fixes it. SeedVR2 and friends sharpen what is already there; they cannot synthesise facial structure that was never generated.

The fix: crop to the face so it fills the frame, let H3 re-generate it at LOW denoise so it stays frame-aligned, then composite back.

nodes.title: DENOISE - read before changing
widgets_values:
DENOISE - THE CRITICAL DIAL

DO NOT carry values over from SDXL-family models. H3 is FLOW MATCHING with a large sigma shift, so the same number means something very different.

sigma = shift*t / (1 + (shift-1)*t)

At the default shift of 12:
  denoise 0.02 -> effective 0.197
  denoise 0.05 -> effective 0.387
  denoise 0.15 -> effective ~0.68
  denoise 0.25 -> effective 0.800

This graph ships denoise 0.40 as a BASE, because it is not applied flat. The H3 Per-Frame Denoise node scales it DOWN per frame by face size: small faces keep close to the full 0.40 and get synthesised, large faces drop to ~0.35x of it and keep the detail they already have.

Base and scaling are tuned TOGETHER. If you bypass the per-frame node, drop the base a long way (0.15-0.25) or every large face gets rewritten.

Too low: nothing changes.
Too high: the head starts drifting relative to the body - a content problem no mask can hide.

NOTE steps and denoise are INDEPENDENT. BasicScheduler builds a (steps/denoise)-long full-range schedule and keeps the lowest steps+1 sigmas, so 8 steps with the turbo LoRA this graph ships is both fast and gentle.

Do NOT use SplitSigmas for this - on a short schedule at shift 12 even the last split point is already sigma 0.800.

nodes.title: Temporal Flow Average Parameter Guide
widgets_values:
## Temporal Flow Average

| Parameter | Description |
|---------|------|
| `window_size` | Frames to average per side (2 = 5 total) |
| `weight_decay` | Temporal weight decay (lower = stronger averaging) |
| `flow_model` | memfof / raft_small / raft_large |
| `flow_iterations` | Flow refinement iters (memfof: 8, raft: 20) |
| `color_threshold` | Per-pixel color diff threshold (anti-ghosting) |
| `scene_threshold` | Scene change threshold (lower = more sensitive) |
| `batch_size` | MEMFOF batch size (higher = faster, more VRAM) |

### Recommended Settings
- **AI video** (Seedance, Kling, etc.)
  - window: `2-3`, decay: `0.7`
- **Live action** (film grain)
  - window: `3-5`, decay: `0.6`
- **Fast motion**
  - window: `1-2`, decay: `0.9`
- **scene_threshold**: 0.03~0.06 (too low may skip denoising)
- **batch_size**: `24` recommended for RTX 5090 32GB at 720p

nodes.title: Selective Denoise Parameter Guide
widgets_values:
## Selective Denoise
Independent per-channel blending of original and clean in color space

| Parameter | Description |
|---------|------|
| `chroma_strength` | Chroma denoising strength (0~1) |
| `luma_strength` | Luma denoising strength (0~1) |
| `color_space` | YCbCr / HSV / LAB |
| `clamp_output` | Clamp output to [0,1] |

### Tips
- **Chroma flicker only**: chroma `1.0`, luma `0.0`
- **Full denoise**: chroma `1.0`, luma `1.0`
- **Preserve luma recommended**: AI video has little brightness variation, keep luma low
- Setting both to 1.0 gives the same result as the Temporal Flow Average clean output. Adjust based on how much detail smearing is acceptable

nodes.title: Why per-frame crop
widgets_values:
PER-FRAME CROPPING IS MANDATORY

A single fixed crop is sized by the widest frame. On a push-in the face is then STILL SMALL inside that crop - on exactly the frames that needed help. The benefit vanishes where it matters.

So the crop SIZE varies per frame, holding the face at a constant fraction of every crop (crop_factor). Every crop is then resized to ONE canvas, because H3 generates a single fixed WxH for a whole sequence.

Result: the face is always large in H3's input, however small it was in the source.

SMOOTHING
size_smooth_window (51) is deliberately larger than smooth_window (21). Size jitter makes the crop breathe, which changes the resample factor every frame and reads as shimmer.

gaussian beats savgol here - polynomial fits preserve sharp features by design, which is the opposite of what you want.

nodes.title: Canvas size
widgets_values:
CANVAS SIZE

canvas_mode decides the resolution H3 generates at:

  manual            - use canvas_width/height exactly as typed
  auto_no_downscale - size from the LARGEST crop in the clip, so no frame is
                      ever downscaled. Can get expensive on clips containing
                      close-ups.
  auto_capped_768   - same, but clamped to 768 (H3's native short edge, and a
                      sane VRAM ceiling). This is what ships here.

canvas_w / canvas_h are WIRED into the H3 node's width/height on purpose. In the auto modes the tracker chooses the size, and if the H3 node disagrees the latent shapes differ and injection refuses. Do not retype them by hand.

Watch the tracker's report for "magnification < 1.0x": that means the crop is being DOWNSCALED into the canvas and real detail is being thrown away. Raise the canvas, or skip the clip if it is close-up throughout.

Cost scales with canvas AREA x frames, so 768 is 2.25x the latent tokens of 512.
